# Herdr selection list: gate background/foreground sync on DB-update check before spawning wl commands

## Problem statement

The Herdr work-item selection list spawns a burst of `wl` CLI processes on a fixed cadence — background `wl sync` every 60s plus a full refresh (`wl next`, 2× `wl list` mandatory subsets, expanded-children fetches) on every 30s auto-refresh tick — **regardless of whether the worklog database changed**. When the pane is idle (no agents writing, no remote activity), each cycle wastes 3–5 process spawns and a full git sync round-trip for zero visible change.

## Users

- **Herdr users running the selection list with auto-refresh/auto-sync on** — want the list to stay current without constant background `wl` process churn (spawn overhead, git fetch/pull/merge/push, lock contention with other panes).
- **Multi-pane / multi-agent setups** — the reduction in unnecessary `wl sync` invocations reduces lock-storm pressure between panes and cross-process DB churn.

Example user stories:
- As a Herdr user with an idle backlog, I want the selection list to avoid spawning any `wl` commands when nothing changed, so my machine isn't churning processes and git round-trips every 30–60s.
- As a Herdr user, I want background sync to still run at least once per configurable window (default 60s) even when nothing changed locally, so I still receive remote changes pushed by other machines.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. On an auto-refresh tick, when the worklog DB has not changed since the last refresh cycle, the pane spawns **zero** `wl` processes for that tick (no `wl next`, no `wl list`, no children fetches, no `wl sync`, no action-count fetch).
2. On an auto-sync tick, `wl sync` is skipped when (a) the DB has not changed since the last cycle **and** (b) the last successful sync is fresher than the configurable max-staleness cap (default 60s). If either condition fails, the sync runs (subject to the existing heartbeat / single-flight / `--if-idle` guards).
3. The max-staleness cap is configurable via the Herdr settings file (e.g. new `maxSyncStalenessMs` setting, default `60000`), clamped to a sane minimum like the sync interval clamp.
4. Manual user actions — `S` (sync) and `r` (refresh) keypresses — always run, ignoring the gate.
5. The very first cycle after pane start always runs (no prior "last seen" signal), and any failure to read the DB-change signal fails **open** (the cycle runs), so the list can never go stale due to a signal-read error.
6. The existing cross-instance heartbeat (`last-sync-time`), single-flight, and `--if-idle` guards remain in place for syncs that do run.
7. Unit tests cover: gate skip/run decisions for refresh and sync ticks (changed/unchanged DB, stale/fresh last-sync, manual override, first-cycle, fail-open), plus the new setting's parse/clamp behavior.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The Herdr plugin package (`packages/herdr`) has **zero npm dependencies** and intentionally duplicates small shared helpers per TUI (decision Q2c in WL-0MS8W5LTW006YZ4B) — a small pure helper duplicating the counter-read logic is consistent with this pattern.
- The DB-change signal must be cheap (a file read or two) and must NOT spawn a `wl` process itself — that is the whole point of the gate.
- The signal must be cross-process stable: the wl CLI read cache (F2) deliberately avoids SQLite file mtimes because "the SQLite files are rewritten by the app on every open/close cycle… file-based fingerprints are not stable across processes" (`src/read-cache.ts`). The gate must not produce false "changed" signals from the pane's own reads.
- Do not change wl CLI sync behavior itself; the incremental-sync work (WL-0MSAKUBKW006FN8Q) is separate scope.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `runWorklistTui` registers two scheduler tasks: `refresh` (every `refreshIntervalMs`, default 30s, always calls `doRefresh(false)` → spawns read commands) and `sync` (every `syncIntervalMs`, default 60s, calls `doSync(true, heartbeatTtlMs)` then `doRefresh(false)`). Plus a `resume-poll` task that calls `doRefresh(true)` on hidden→visible transition.
- `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts` — `runSync` spawns `wl sync` fire-and-forget with cross-instance heartbeat skip (`last-sync-time` marker, `isSyncHeartbeatFresh`), single-flight guard, and `--if-idle`.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — all read commands (`wl next`, `wl list`, children, action-count) go through `runWl`; the CLI serves many from its on-disk read cache (F2), but a process spawn still occurs per command.
- `src/read-cache.ts` / `src/read-cache-cli.ts` — the wl CLI maintains a monotonic per-worklog-dir **state counter** (`~/.cache/wl/state/<sha256(worklogDir)>.json`, `{ "state": N }`), bumped by every wl write command and by post-sync invalidation (`invalidateCacheForWrite`). This is the natural "DB changed" signal: cross-process, stable across reads, and already the CLI's freshness authority.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — typed settings JSON with clamped intervals; `syncIntervalMs` has a 60s minimum clamp.
- Manual `S`/`r` keypresses dispatch to `doSync()` / `doRefresh(true)` unconditionally.

## Desired change

- Add a small pure module in `packages/herdr` (e.g. `db-change.ts`) that:
  - resolves the wl cache dir (mirroring `resolveCacheDir()` precedence: `WL_CACHE_DIR` → `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/wl` → `~/.cache/wl`);
  - reads the state counter for the resolved worklog dir (`state/<sha256(worklogDir)>.json`), returning the counter value (0 when absent); and
  - exposes a `DbChangeTracker`/helper that remembers the last-seen counter per pane and answers `dbChangedSinceLastCycle()` (fail-open: any read error ⇒ true).
- Gate the scheduler tasks in `runWorklistTui`:
  - `refresh` tick: skip (spawn nothing) when the DB is unchanged since the last cycle.
  - `sync` tick: skip `wl sync` when DB unchanged **and** last successful sync (heartbeat marker) is within the configurable max-staleness cap; otherwise run `doSync` + `doRefresh` as today.
  - `resume-poll` hidden→visible transition: apply the same DB-change gate (list content is identical when nothing changed).
  - Manual `S`/`r` paths unchanged (always run).
- Add the configurable cap to settings (e.g. `maxSyncStalenessMs`, default 60s, clamped ≥1s or aligned with the sync-interval clamp) and pass it through `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`.
- Keep all existing guards (heartbeat, single-flight, `--if-idle`) for syncs that do run.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/db-change.ts` — NEW: pure DB-change signal reader (wl cache-dir resolution + state-counter read + last-seen tracker), fail-open.
- `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts` — expose/adapt staleness helpers (reuse `readSyncHeartbeatMs`) so the sync tick can decide "DB unchanged AND sync fresh ⇒ skip".
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — wire the gate into the `refresh` / `sync` / `resume-poll` scheduler tasks; manual `S`/`r` untouched.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — new `maxSyncStalenessMs` setting (default `60000`) with clamping.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — pass the new setting into `runWorklistTui`.
- `src/read-cache.ts` — read-only reference for the counter-file format/path derivation (no changes expected).
- Tests: `packages/herdr/src/db-change.test.ts` (NEW), plus updates to `auto-sync.test.ts`, `worklist.test.ts`, `settings.test.ts`.

## Related work

- `WL-0MSGAEJQA005QG3W` — Cross-instance sync heartbeat (F3): the `last-sync-time` marker and heartbeat TTL this change composes with. Completed.
- `WL-0MSAB7ZUC004SK7E` — wl sync lock storm: auto-sync single-flight / `--if-idle` guards; gating reduces spawn pressure further. Completed.
- `WL-0MSGAEC5N006W5QA` — wl CLI read cache (F2) with the state-counter fingerprint this gate reuses as its signal. Completed.
- `WL-0MSAKUBKW006FN8Q` — Incremental sync: only export/push changed work items (CLI-side; explicitly out of scope here). Open.
- `WL-0MS8W5LTW006YZ4B` — Smart-selection duplication decision (Q2c): precedent for duplicating a small pure helper into the Herdr package. Completed.
- `docs/dev/release-process.md` — release workflow (no code impact; doc reference).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Remote-pull latency (accepted tradeoff, user-confirmed):** skipping `wl sync` when the DB is unchanged delays pulling remote changes until the next sync that does run. Bounded by the max-staleness cap (default 60s) so remote freshness is never worse than the cap.
- **Signal completeness:** the state counter is bumped by wl CLI writes and post-sync invalidation. External tools writing the SQLite DB directly (not via wl) would not bump it — mitigated by the staleness cap, which forces a periodic sync regardless. Assumed acceptable.
- **Configurable cap naming/units:** `maxSyncStalenessMs` in ms, default 60000, clamped to ≥1s (aligned with `heartbeatTtlForInterval`'s clamp) — exact name subject to implementer/plan review.
- **Scope-creep guard:** incremental sync (WL-0MSAKUBKW006FN8Q), event-driven window subscription (WL-0MSHB7DHO004RHBJ), and WAL checkpointing (WL-0MSG8EG7P002MX2I) are tracked separately and must NOT be pulled into this work item.
- **Behavioral parity:** when the DB IS changing, cadence must match today (no additional latency); only the no-change case adds skipping.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (asked 2026-08-07): "If the local DB hasn't changed, should the background `wl sync` also be skipped? That means remote changes pushed by other machines would only be pulled when local activity bumps the counter (or via manual `S`). Acceptable — or should the sync path stay ungated while only the refresh reads are skipped?" — Answer (user): "Partially acceptable. wl sync can be skipped if no local DB changes. However, it should not go more than 1 minute (configurable) without being run." Source: interactive reply. → Implemented as AC2/AC3: sync is gated by (DB unchanged AND last successful sync within configurable max-staleness cap, default 60s).
- Q2 (asked 2026-08-07): "Should manual refresh (`r`) and manual sync (`S`) always run regardless of the check? (My assumption: yes — user-initiated actions always execute.)" — Answer (user): "yes". Source: interactive reply. → Implemented as AC4.
- Q3 (asked 2026-08-07, /skill:find-related): "Which work items are related?" — Research: the find-related script (`find_related.py --work-item-id WL-0MSJ1OLTL009N4IQ`) resolved the wrong worklog store (SorraAgents framework repo) on both runs and returned unrelated items (OpenBrain submission, file-path convention, a-y shortcut). The matches were excluded per the skill's conservative policy (false negatives preferred); the curated Related work section above (verified via `wl show` against the ContextHub store) is authoritative.

# Feature Request: --fields field-selection for wl list / wl search

## Problem statement

wl list and wl search return full work-item records (or compact snippets for search), with no way to request only the fields a caller needs. Full-record dumps are the root cause of token waste documented in SA-0MSLVQMKF000ESPZ (SorraAgents): bare wl list --json = 5.3 MB / 1,861 records; wl list --status completed = 4.9 MB; scripts (ship gates, triage, code-review) download tens-to-hundreds of KB of fields they never read (e.g. full descriptions) when they only need id, title, status, stage, priority.

## User stories

- As a release-gate script, I want wl list --stage in_review --fields id,title,status,stage,needsProducerReview --json so I stop downloading 4.9 MB of descriptions I discard.
- As an agent running /skill:audit, I want a compact project-status query (fields id,title,status,stage,priority) so the worklog overview stays in the low-KB range.
- As a triage helper, I want wl list --priority critical --tags test-failure --fields id,title,description --json so my match heuristics get exactly the fields they need.

## Expected behaviour

- New option on wl list and wl search: --fields comma-separated (e.g. id,title,status,stage,priority).
- Output objects contain ONLY the requested fields (plus id always, for usability); unknown field names are rejected with a clear error listing valid fields.
- wl list and wl search share the same field vocabulary: id, title, description, status, stage, priority, issueType, assignee, tags, createdAt, updatedAt, parentId, needsProducerReview, sortIndex.
- --json output shape unchanged (same keys; omitted fields absent). Human output uses the same projection for concise display.
- -f as shorthand is acceptable; must not clash with existing flags (-F/--format already taken).

## Acceptance criteria

1. wl list --fields id,title --json returns objects with only id/title; verified for filters and bare queries.
2. wl search term --fields id,title,status --json returns compact objects with only those fields.
3. Invalid field names produce a non-zero exit and a clear error listing valid fields.
4. Output size reduction verified: wl list --stage in_review --fields id,title --json is smaller than the full-record equivalent (target: >=90% reduction for the completed-status case cited above).
5. Existing output without --fields is unchanged (backward compatible); full test suite passes.

## Plan

### Child Work Items (dependency-ordered)

1. **WL-0MT5L3BGA001MKOP** - Create pickFields() projection helper module
2. **WL-0MT5L4MGL000Z43Y** - Write unit tests for pickFields projection helper (depends on 1)
3. **WL-0MT5L55AQ002WTGQ** - Add --fields option to wl list (depends on 1, 2)
4. **WL-0MT5L6G88006N4WD** - Add --fields option to wl search (depends on 1, 2)
5. **WL-0MT5L6TLQ004NDLK** - Integration test: end-to-end --fields flag verification (depends on 3, 4)

### Implementation Approach

1. Create packages/shared/src/fields.ts with pickFields(item, fields?) helper
2. Add fields?: string to ListOptions and SearchOptions in cli-types.ts
3. Apply pickFields projection in list.ts before JSON output
4. Apply pickFields projection in search.ts before JSON output
5. Write unit tests and integration tests

### Review Stages Summary

1. Requirements & AC alignment: All 5 ACs map to user stories and expected behaviour. No gaps or contradictions.
2. Completeness: Description has all required sections. Key files are valid.
3. Sequencing & dependencies: Test items before implementation items. Dependencies properly set.
4. Scope sizing: Small effort, Low risk - appropriate for scope.
5. Acceptance & testability: All ACs are testable with clear pass/fail criteria.
6. Polish & handoff: Plan is copy-pasteable and actionable.

## Plan Changelog

- 2026-08-23T09:09Z - Plan created with 5 child work items. Pre-check: Small effort, Low risk. All review stages passed.

## Appendix

- Q: Should --fields support nested field access (e.g. auditResult.readyToClose)? Answer (plan agent): No. The work item scope is flat field selection only. Nested access can be added later if needed. Final: not in scope.
- Q: Should -f shorthand be supported? Answer (plan agent): Yes, but -f is not taken in either list or search. Final: -f can be added as shorthand.

# Intake Brief: Sync — Regression Guard

## Problem Statement

When `wl sync` merges remote state that is newer than local, it can silently import regressions: fields the local store had set to non-default values (e.g. `effort: 'Small'`, `status: completed`) get overwritten with defaults by a stale/divergent second store, as observed Aug 6–10, 2026 on the llm worklog ref.

## Users

- **Primary**: Operators of multi-store worklog setups — anyone running more than one `wl sync` instance against the same remote.
- **Secondary**: Producers/reviewers whose audit results (status/stage transitions) are silently reverted by stale syncs.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. During merge, for each incoming remote item with a newer `updatedAt` than local, detect regressions where a field moves from a non-default value to its default on the fields that participate in the merge: `status`/`stage` (non-default → default, e.g. `completed/in_review` → `open/idea`), `priority` (non-default → default), and `assignee` (set → unset).

   **`effort`/`risk` (producer resolution, 2026-08-23): stay PERMANENTLY EXCLUDED from the merge field lists** — ping-pong prevention by construction. A remote `effort: ''` / `risk: ''` never enters the merge; local non-default values are always kept. The guard additionally REPORTS any attempted effort/risk regression (remote non-empty → default) as a protected conflict (local kept, nothing imported) for observability, but no override path is needed for these two fields since they cannot be imported through the merge.
2. On detecting a regression, `wl sync` refuses to import that item's regressed fields: reports the conflict (item id, field, old local value, new remote default value) and keeps the local value. An explicit override flag (`--accept-regressions` or equivalent) allows the operator to accept the regression.
3. Genuine concurrent edits (both stores changed different non-default fields, or both changed the same field to different non-default values) still merge and re-timestamp exactly as today — this guard must NOT change legitimate conflict resolution.
4. The regression guard applies only to the `import()`/merge path used by `wl sync` — it does NOT affect explicit user `wl update` commands, which remain authoritative.
5. Unit tests cover: (a) newer remote with `effort: ''` against local `effort: 'Small'` → local kept (exclusion by construction), conflict REPORTED as protected, remote value NOT imported; (b) newer remote with `status: open` against local `completed` → refused, local kept, conflict reported; (c) both sides non-default differing → normal merge + re-timestamp (no regression path — guard must NOT alter legitimate conflict resolution); (d) override flag accepts the regression for merge-participating fields only; (e) `--dry-run` reports the same refusals.
6. Manual verification: sync against the known commit `5fc880a` (effort/risk cleared) → regressions refused and reported; sync against `54b1375` (restored values) → no regression flags.

## Constraints

- Must not change behavior for legitimate concurrent edits — the guard is regression-only, not conflict-resolution.
- Must be deterministic: dry-run and normal sync report the same refusals.
- Does NOT prevent a second store from pushing — it prevents the primary store from absorbing regressive state.
- Complements the identity gate (WL-0MSOYWWS4009HTCB) — the identity gate catches the writer; this guard catches the damage even if the writer's identity is unknown.

## Existing State

The merge functions (`mergeSameTimestampItems`, `mergeDifferentTimestampItems` in `src/sync.ts`) already implement a non-default-preference heuristic: when one side has a non-default value and the other has a default, the non-default is preserved. The `isDefaultValue` helper in `src/sync/merge-utils.ts` classifies empty strings, `undefined`, and empty arrays as defaults.

The merge field arrays include `status`, `stage`, `priority`, and `assignee` — these fields **already** keep the local non-default value when the remote sends a default (via the `!localIsDefault && remoteIsDefault` branch). They do **not** produce an explicit regression report — the local value is silently kept.

The merge field arrays do **not** include `effort` or `risk` — these fields are never merged at all; the local value is always preserved regardless of the remote.

**Contradiction — RESOLVED (producer decision, 2026-08-23)**: The 13-field merge list currently excludes `effort`/`risk` (code-confirmed), yet the original ACs listed them as regression targets. Producer directive: *"The goal is to prevent ping-pong — do what you need to."* Resolution: **Reading A** — `effort`/`risk` remain excluded from the merge lists; adding them to the merge would re-introduce the ping-pong (the DB re-timestamp amplifier in `hasWorkItemChanged` already tracks these fields, so a single unguarded import becomes the newest record and propagates). The guard therefore targets the merge-participating fields (`status`/`stage`/`priority`/`assignee`), and `effort`/`risk` regressions are reported as protected (local kept). Effort/risk merge-participation is a non-goal.

## Desired Change

Add a regression detection layer on top of the merge path that:
- Identifies fields regressing from non-default → default in newer remote state, for the merge-participating fields: `status`/`stage`/`priority`/`assignee`
- Reports conflicts with details (item id, field, old value, new value)
- Refuses to import regressed fields (keeping local) unless overridden (`--accept-regressions`, merge-participating fields only)
- Preserves all existing merge behavior for non-regression cases
- Reports (without importing) attempted `effort`/`risk` regressions as protected — these fields remain excluded from the merge lists (non-goal: adding them back)

## Risks & Assumptions

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|--------|------------|
| Regression detection logic breaks existing merge behavior | High | Unit tests must verify non-regression cases still merge correctly (AC3) |
| Scope creep: "regression" definition might be too broad (e.g., should a valid transition like `in_progress → open` count as regression?) | Medium | Strict definition: only non-default → default transitions count |
| Override flag (`--accept-regressions`) could be misused, allowing silent data loss | Medium | Require explicit flag; report what was accepted in output |
| **DECIDED**: effort/risk must NOT be added to the merge list | — | Producer resolution 2026-08-23: adding them re-introduces ping-pong (DB re-timestamp amplifier `hasWorkItemChanged` tracks these fields; one unguarded import becomes the newest record) |
| `isDefaultValue` may not correctly identify defaults for all fields (e.g., custom stages) | Low | Only built-in defaults (`open`, `idea`, `medium`, empty strings) are guarded; custom stages fall through to normal merge |
| **Scope-creep risk**: The guard could be extended to "merge strategies" or general conflict-policy work — those are separate concerns. | Medium | Record as future work items; do not implement here |

**Assumptions**:
- The `isDefaultValue` function correctly classifies all default values for the fields in question
- Regression detection can be cleanly layered on top of existing merge logic without restructuring
- The operator will accept a new CLI flag for override

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/sync.ts` — `mergeSameTimestampItems`, `mergeDifferentTimestampItems`: add regression detection alongside the existing merge logic (field lists UNCHANGED for `effort`/`risk` — exclusion is the ping-pong prevention)
- `src/sync/merge-utils.ts` — `isDefaultValue`: may need no changes (already classifies empties as defaults)
- `src/commands/sync.ts` — CLI flag for `--accept-regressions`, conflict reporting in output
- `tests/sync-regression-guard.test.ts` — new test file for regression detection scenarios

## Related Work

| ID | Title | Relationship |
|----|-------|-------------|
| WL-0MSOYWWS4009HTCB | Sync: identity gate — refuse merge of foreign/empty-author commits | Related: same root cause incident (Aug 2026 llm worklog pollution); identity gate catches the writer, regression guard catches the damage |
| WL-0MSORD6HC005QVZX | Sync: do not change updatedAt on whitespace-only changes | Completed; orthogonal concern |
| WL-0MKVZ510K1XHJ7B3 | Sync & data integrity | Completed; foundational sync merge logic |
| WL-0MSUEOAQO0081TJH | Wire identity gate into wl sync + config flag + sync-point persistence | Completed; identity gate now wired into sync |

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions

- **Q (auto-resolved by code inspection)**: The description says "the 13-field merge list currently excludes effort/risk" — the code confirms `effort` and `risk` are NOT in the merge field arrays. Does this mean: (a) the ACs about effort/risk are stale and should be removed, or (b) the description is outdated and effort/risk regressions need explicit detection and reporting? → **Answer (producer, 2026-08-23): "The goal is to prevent ping-pong — do what you need to." Interpreted as Reading A: effort/risk stay excluded from the merge lists (prevention by construction); the guard targets merge-participating fields (status/stage/priority/assignee) and reports protected effort/risk conflict attempts without importing them. Adding effort/risk to the merge is a non-goal.** Source: interactive reply, this intake session (2026-08-23).
- **Q**: What is the exact override flag name? The ACs mention `--accept-regressions` or equivalent. → **Flagged for producer confirmation.**
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MS8XLS0Z00759QI** – Pi TUI tools.ts: smart selection (helper copy + fetch merge + apply) (completed)
- **WL-0MSVRMAWM007QNR5** – Downtime worker: parseLlamaStatus rejects numeric slot_id — every poll fail-closes to busy, zero dispatches (completed)
- **WL-0MSHWHFAK005WKDB** – [test-failure] defaultSettings has default browseItemCount of 10 — failing test (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: ac3, accept, acceptance, accepted, accepts (+231 more)
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: ac3, accept, acceptance, accepted, accepts (+204 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: accept, accepts, add, adding, affect (+191 more)

# Herdr selection list: let list take as much space as it needs; metadata fills the rest and scrolls (WL-0MSQ44MDX008U69J)

## Headline

Flip the space priority in the Herdr worklist pane: the selection list may use up to the full available pane height (including its header lines), and the metadata section fills whatever space remains — expanding when the list is short, sitting below the fold (revealed by scrolling down) when the list is long — scrolling internally when its content overflows.

## Problem statement

The metadata section below the selection list currently reserves a fixed 20–40% of the pane height (`computeMetadataPanelHeight`), squeezing the list. When the list needs more vertical space than it is allotted, it scrolls and the header/top lines scroll off the top of the pane, even though the metadata section below is eating rows the list could use. The metadata section should no longer force the list to scroll off the top.

## Users

- **Herdr users (human and AI agent)** browsing the work item list in a pane, who want the selection list — including its header line — to use as much vertical space as it needs, up to the maximum available, so items don't scroll off the top prematurely.

### User stories

- As a Herdr user, when the list is long, I want the list (header + items) to take up to the full pane height so I can see as many items as possible without the top scrolling off.
- As a Herdr user, when the list is short, I want the metadata section to expand into the leftover space so the pane still shows the selected item's metadata.
- As a Herdr user, when the list fills the full pane, I want to scroll the pane down to expose the rest of the list and then the metadata section, with the initial view starting at the top of the selection list.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **List takes as much space as it needs, up to the max available**: The selection list (header line + items + group separators + footer) can use up to the maximum number of vertical lines available in the pane (pane rows minus the reserved notification row). The metadata section no longer reserves a fixed 20–40% share that forces the list to scroll.
2. **Initial view at top**: When the list fills the full vertical space, the view starts at the top of the selection list (header + first items visible). Scrolling the pane down exposes the rest of the list and, at the end, the metadata section.
3. **Metadata fills the rest**: When the list content is shorter than the available height, the metadata section expands to fill the leftover space below the list.
4. **Metadata scrolls if necessary**: When the metadata content overflows the space allotted to it, it scrolls independently using the existing `m`/`M` keys and `metaScrollOffset` (with the existing `[m/M scroll NN%]` indicator), and the selection-driven reset behaviour is preserved.
5. **No regression**: Keyboard navigation (arrows/j/k, PgUp/PgDn, g/G, wrap), stage filtering, group separators, auto-refresh, code-freeze banner, and the reserved notification row continue to work; rendered output never exceeds the pane's `rows` budget.
6. **Testing**: Unit tests cover (a) list height = min(content need, max available), (b) metadata expansion when the list is short, (c) reveal-by-scroll when the list fills the pane and initial view at top, (d) metadata scroll clamping under the new layout, and (e) the output line-count invariant (≤ `rows`).
7. **Docs**: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is **excluded** — managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- Plugin-local change in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`; no `wl` CLI or backend schema changes.
- The rendered output must never exceed the pane's `rows` budget (last row reserved for the notification line; group-separator accounting must not overflow) — the invariant from WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO must hold.
- Preserve existing keyboard bindings: `m`/`M` for metadata scrolling, and all list-navigation keys unchanged.

As an operator, I do not want the herdr downtime worker to inhibit dispatch based on the GLOBAL active_query signal when the proxy serves the local-only signal, so that remote/cloud streams never block local downtime dispatch. The backward-compatibility fallback to the global `active_query` for pre-fix proxies must be removed.

## Background

- `isIdleStatus`/`globalIdleChecks` in packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts: `const queryActive = status.local_active_query !== undefined ? status.local_active_query : status.active_query;` — the fallback to `active_query` exists for proxies that predate the `local_active_queries` counter (LP-0MSL2ZLLS009RVKR, delivered in WL-0MSL2ZQIF006QB4Q).
- The global `active_query` is true whenever ANY request is in flight — local AND remote provider streams. Remote streams keep it true while the local model is idle with free slots, so the fallback can block legitimate downtime dispatch (RCA WL-0MSK9TUCA00206M7).
- The local-only signal (`local_active_query`) is the correct busy signal for the local model.

## Design notes

- Remove the `local_active_query !== undefined ? ... : active_query` fallback; use only `local_active_query`.
- Fail-closed question to resolve: is a MISSING `local_active_query` now treated as busy (no dispatch) or idle (dispatch)? Decision: treat a missing signal as busy (fail-closed, consistent with the rest of the worker) — a pre-fix proxy must not cause dispatch on an unverifiable signal.
- parseLlamaStatus currently accepts an absent `local_active_query` (`undefined`); a work item must decide whether absence becomes null (busy) or a documented explicit non-dispatch.
- Update parseLlamaStatus doc + isIdleStatus/globalIdleChecks comments (LP-0MSL2ZLLS009RVKR reference).

## Acceptance criteria

1. `globalIdleChecks` uses ONLY `local_active_query` once present in the payload; the `active_query` fallback is removed.
2. A payload WITHOUT `local_active_query` fails closed: the worker treats the status as busy (no dispatch) and the behaviour is documented — no silent degraded dispatch on pre-fix proxies.
3. Remote/cloud streams (global active_query true, local false) are never a dispatch inhibitor.
4. Test suite covers: local_active_query present (both values), local_active_query absent (busy), and the removal of the fallback branch.

# Ensure only single audit active during downtime dispatch

## Problem statement

During downtime dispatching through the leader, only a single audit should ever be active at any one time. The dispatch logic must check for existing active audits (dispatched but not yet completed) and skip dispatching another audit if one is already in progress, ensuring audits are strictly sequential rather than allowing fan-out.

## Users

- **Operator running multiple herdr instances** — wants audit work to progress deterministically, one at a time, without competing audits consuming LLM capacity.
- **Operator relying on audit results for release decisions** — needs audit outcomes to be reliable and complete; concurrent audits increase the risk of missed findings.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Audit sequential enforcement** — Before dispatching an audit-tier item, the dispatcher checks whether any audit-tier item is currently `in_progress` (dispatched but not yet completed/reviewed). If one exists, the audit tier is skipped and the dispatcher falls through to the next tier.
2. **Leader-only check** — Only the elected leader performs the active-audit check; non-leader instances do not dispatch audits at all (unchanged behavior).
3. **Check mechanism** — The dispatcher queries the worklog for any audit-tier item (completed/in_review candidates) that has a corresponding dispatch entry in `downtime-dispatches.log` with kind `audit`. If the dispatched audit entry is older than a stale threshold (2 hours), it is treated as stale and ignored (audit pane may have crashed without updating the work item).
4. **Active audit blocks new dispatch** — If an active (non-stale) audit is found, the audit tier is skipped and dispatch falls through to the implement tier. The skip reason `audit-in-flight` is logged for observability.
5. **Existing guards preserved** — The single-flight guard (`dispatchInFlight`), CAS claim, dispatched-marker exclusion, and code-freeze gate continue to work unchanged.
6. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Audit tier only** — this constraint applies only to the audit dispatch tier; implement/plan/intake tiers are unaffected.
- **Existing single-flight guard** — the in-process `dispatchInFlight` guard remains in place; this adds a cross-idle-period guard (prevents re-dispatch on the next idle tick while a previous audit is still running).
- **Coordination file aware** — in the leader-election refactor context, the check must consider audits dispatched by any instance (not just the current instance), using the coordination file or dispatch log as the source of truth.
- **Fail-safe** — if the active-audit check cannot complete (e.g., worklog query fails), the dispatcher falls through to the next tier rather than blocking all dispatch.

## Existing state

- `dispatchDowntimeWork` dispatches audit-tier items via `dispatchClaimedTier(deps, 'audit', ...)`.
- The `dispatchInFlight` guard prevents concurrent dispatch calls within the same idle period.
- CAS claim moves dispatched items to `in_progress`, removing them from `wl next`/`wl list` selection.
- Dispatched markers in `downtime-dispatches.log` track dispatched items with kind and timestamp.
- The audit tier runs first, before implement/plan/intake tiers.
- Under the leader-election refactor (WL-0MST3OJ8S0001ROL), only the leader dispatches, but multiple idle periods could span across a running audit.

## Desired change

1. **Active audit check** — Before selecting an audit candidate, query whether any audit-tier item is currently active (dispatched and `in_progress`). This can be done by: (a) scanning the dispatched-marker log for recent audit dispatches where the item is still `in_progress`, or (b) querying the worklog for `in_progress` items that match audit-tier criteria.
2. **Audit tier skip** — If an active audit is found, skip the audit tier and proceed to the implement tier (unchanged fallback behavior).
3. **Logging** — Log the skip reason (`audit-in-flight`) for observability.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `dispatchDowntimeWork`: add active-audit check before `getNextAuditCandidate`; skip audit tier if active audit found; log skip reason.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — possibly a new dep method `getActiveAudits(cwd)` or reuse existing dispatched-marker logic.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` — tests: audit skipped when one active, audit dispatched when none active, active-audit check failure falls through gracefully.

## Related work

- **WL-0MST3OJ8S0001ROL** — Refactor Downtime Dispatcher: leader election with shared coordination file (open, plan_complete) — the primary context; this constraint applies to the leader-only dispatch model.
- **WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG** — Allow /skill:audit on complete/in_review items without a valid audit (completed) — establishes the audit tier.
- **WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY** — Downtime dispatcher triggers multiple identical sessions (completed) — parent for dispatched-marker exclusion.

### Related work (automated report)

- **WL-0MT32F908002YFFA** — Downtime dispatch: recover items stranded by marker-write-failed or spawn-failed (open) — directly relevant to stale-audit timeout design; a crashed audit pane that fails to update the work item state is the scenario the timeout protects against.
- **WL-0MSN3FWV5008KQE9** — Herdr plugin: activity-gated proxy mode switching (completed) — proxy idle/busy semantics relevant to dispatch timing.
- **WL-0ML7QRBQR183KXPB** — Auto-unblock on dependency changes (completed) — dependency resolution patterns may inform how active-audit detection handles blocked items.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** An audit is considered "active" from the moment it is dispatched (marked in `downtime-dispatches.log`) until the item transitions from `in_progress` to a terminal state (`completed`/`in_review` with a fresh audit, or reverted to `completed/in_review` for re-audit).
- **Assumption:** The dispatch log or worklog query is fast enough to not impact dispatch latency (should be sub-second for typical worklog sizes).

- **Risk:** The active-audit check adds complexity to the dispatch loop. Mitigation: keep the check simple (one worklog query or log scan) and fail-open (skip audit tier on query failure).
- **Scope-creep guard:** Extending this constraint to implement/plan/intake tiers is out of scope. Only audit-tier sequentialization is required.
- **Risk (leader-election context):** Multiple instances could have stale active-audit entries from crashed instances. Mitigation: the check should use the coordination file or dispatch log timestamps to detect stale entries.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Should the single-audit constraint apply only to audits, or to all dispatch tiers?" — Answer (user): "Audit only. Implement/plan/intake are not affected." Source: interactive reply.
- Q2: "How should we detect an 'active' audit? By worklog status or dispatch log?" — Answer (user): "Check for audit-tier items that are dispatched but not yet completed — use the dispatched markers or worklog query. The check must work in the leader-election context." Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "What happens if the active-audit check fails?" — Answer (user): "Fail-open: skip the audit tier and fall through to implement. Do not block all dispatch." Source: interactive reply.
- Q4: "Should there be a timeout on active audits? (e.g., if an audit pane crashes, the item stays in_progress forever)" — Answer (user): "Yes — add a stale-audit timeout. If an audit dispatch entry is older than a reasonable threshold (e.g., 2 hours), treat it as stale and allow re-dispatch." Source: interactive reply.
data.title: Ensure only single audit active during downtime dispatch

## Goal

The ship skill release gate (`check-audit-gate.js`) hard-blocks the release when an audit report contains markers the transient-detection regex doesn't recognize — specifically `"semaphore busy: no slot free within 0.0s (max_workers=1)"` (audit-infra concurrency failure) and `"Pi model output could not be parsed"`. These are transient infra failures, not genuine "not ready to close" verdicts, but the gate treats them as genuine and blocks with exit code 6.

## Evidence (observed during dev→main release attempt, 2026-08-25)

- `TIMEOUT_TRANSIENT_PATTERNS` in `check-audit-gate.js` only matches:
  1. `\btime(?:d)?\s*outs?\b` ("timed out", "time out", "timeout(s)")
  2. `provider\s+(?:error|stop\s+reason)` ("Pi provider error: ...")
  3. `script\s+execution\s+failure` (FailureNotice banner)
- Items whose audits failed with "Audit concurrency limit reached: semaphore 'audit' busy: no slot free within 0.0s (max_workers=1). Retry when fewer audits are running." did **not** match any pattern → gate classified them "Audit verdict: not ready to close" (BLOCKING) instead of transient (warning, non-blocking).
- Same classification hole applies to "Pi model output could not be parsed — raw output logged" (the local-proxy output parse failure).
- Concretely blocked: WL-0MSKSMRFP001Q3XU (three successive audits failed deterministically with the semaphore-busy diagnostic; identical content fingerprint each run, slot pool verified free, no other audit running) and previously WL-0MSQ44MDX008U69J, WL-0MT3PHW4I002SNOV.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. An audit whose stored report contains the semaphore-busy message ("semaphore ... busy: no slot free") is classified as transient (non-blocking, warning) by `check-audit-gate.js` — extend `TIMEOUT_TRANSIENT_PATTERNS` (or the classification logic) with a marker for the audit-infra concurrency failure.
2. An audit whose stored report contains "Pi model output could not be parsed" (with a root-level diagnostic of a transient infra failure) is classified as transient rather than a genuine verdict.
3. The classification change is covered by unit tests in `check-audit-gate.js`'s test suite (new test cases for the semaphore-busy and unparseable-output markers; existing transient tests still pass).
4. `isTimeoutOrTransientAudit` remains conservative: genuine verdicts (e.g. "Ready to close: No" with real AC evidence and no infra-failure markers) stay blocking.

## Notes

- Discovered during release remediation of WL-0MT3FM8VA005XBHE / WL-0MSKSMRFP001Q3XU / WL-0MSQ44MDX008U69J (dev→main ship attempt).
- The semaphore is a flock-based cross-process semaphore (`skill/shared/process_semaphore.py`); slot pool lives at `<XDG_RUNTIME_DIR>/pi-semaphores/audit/` with 5 slot files, auto-released on process exit — the busy failure is a transient acquisition race, not a stuck lock.

## Problem statement

The herdr downtime worker audit tier selects a candidate via `selectAuditCandidate` (freshness checked at selection time), then `dispatchClaimedTier` runs CAS claim → `recordDispatch` (writes the "Auto-dispatched…" work-item comment + rolling marker) → spawn. If **during the interim** — between selection and the comment/spawn — a valid audit was recorded (e.g. a human or another process ran `wl audit-set`), the worker still writes the dispatch comment and spawns a redundant audit pane. The stale/unaudited state it selected no longer exists, so the dispatch is wasted work and the comment is misleading.

Observed (WL-0MT3FLZJ20076X9B): dispatch comment + marker written at 2026-08-24T20:51:49Z while a valid audit existed/landed; a later comment then made the audit appear stale and the item was re-dispatched repeatedly (audit re-recorded 2026-08-25T09:56Z).

RCA: `claimItem` CAS-guards status/stage only (TIER_EXPECTED audit = completed/in_review) — a manual `wl audit-set` does NOT change status/stage, so the claim still succeeds. There is no freshness re-check between selection and `recordDispatch`/spawn. Discovered-from: WL-0MT3FLZJ20076X9B.

## Desired change

In the audit-tier dispatch path, after selecting a candidate and before writing the dispatch comment/marker and spawning, re-check that the item still lacks a fresh audit (`isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` from @worklog/shared/icons). If a fresh audit now exists:
- skip the dispatch entirely (no comment, no marker, no spawn) and fall through to the next tier — treat as "already audited", not "no-candidate"/cooldown and not a strike;
- on a failed spawn (`recordDispatchFailure` / spawn-failed path), do not record/comment a failure trace if a valid audit was recorded during the interim — the pane is moot, not a failure to log as such.

Mirror the same interim freshness re-check in any other dispatcher that comments on audit dispatch (heartbeat does not comment; it invokes the runner directly — verify).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Integration test: select a stale/un-audited candidate, then record a valid audit in the "interim", then verify dispatch downgrades to a no-op (no item comment, no rolling-log `kind=audit` marker, no spawn) and falls through to the next tier without triggering the no-candidate cooldown
- [ ] Integration test: spawn-failure trace (`outcome: spawn-failed`) is NOT appended (and no failure comment) when a valid audit was recorded during the interim
- [ ] A genuinely unaudited item still dispatches exactly as today (comment + marker + spawn)
- [ ] Convention/naming: the interim check is a single dep on the worker boundary (e.g. a `hasFreshAudit(itemId)` dep) so it is testable without wl
- [ ] Full project test suite passes

## Key files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `dispatchClaimedTier` / audit-tier dispatch in `dispatchDowntimeWork` (~lines 1854–1904), `selectAuditCandidate` (~3020), worker deps (~879)
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — wire the interim freshness dep into `createDowntimeDeps` (alongside `getNextAuditCandidate`)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` — interim-freshness integration tests

## Related work

- WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG — audit tier dispatch

# Use markdown rendering in description preview (metadata panel)

## Problem statement

The description preview in the metadata panel shows raw markdown source lines
(up to 3 non-empty lines), with no formatting — headings, bold, links, code,
and lists all render as literal text. The detail view already uses
`renderMarkdown()` for the same content with full styling. Users expect the
preview to convey the same visual information as the detail view.

## Users

- **Herdr operators** browsing the selection list want to quickly gauge what a
  work item is about without opening the detail view. A properly formatted
  preview (with headings, bold, links) communicates meaning much faster than
  raw text.

- **Producers** reviewing items in the list mode need to see structured content
  (e.g., a bolded summary line, a link to a design doc) at a glance.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Markdown rendering** — `buildDescriptionPreview()` is replaced with a
   function that calls `renderMarkdown()` (from `md-viewer.ts`) on the item's
   description, producing styled terminal lines instead of raw source lines.
2. **Available-space layout** — The preview fills available panel space: the
   selection list takes precedence (dynamic layout), the metadata panel fills
   the remainder, and the description preview consumes the full panel height
   (respecting the 3-row minimum only when other metadata lines are present).
3. **Cached rendering** — Rendered output is cached per item (keyed by item ID
   + description hash) so the markdown parser runs only once per selection
   change; on refresh of the same item, the cached output is reused. Cache
   invalidation occurs on item refresh, selection change, and when the
   description is modified externally.
4. **Construct parity** — Headings (h1–h6), bold, italic, strikethrough, links,
   inline code, fenced code blocks, blockquotes, lists (ordered and nested),
   tables, and horizontal rules all render correctly via `renderMarkdown()`.
5. **ANSI safety** — Rendered lines are properly truncated to panel width; ANSI
   sequences are not broken by truncation. No line exceeds the terminal width.
6. **Tests updated** — Existing `formatMetadataPanel` description preview tests
   are updated to cover markdown rendering; new tests verify cache behavior,
   line width safety, and construct rendering.
7. **Backward compatibility** — No visible change to items without descriptions;
   the preview section is omitted when description is missing/blank (unchanged).

## Constraints

- Performance: markdown rendering must not cause frame drops. Caching is
  mandatory.
- The selection list must always retain layout priority — the metadata panel
  never steals rows from the list.
- The metadata panel's minimum height (3 rows) is preserved when there is no
  description.

## Existing state

- `buildDescriptionPreview()` in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` splits the
  description by `
`, takes up to 3 non-empty lines, and renders them with
  simple padding and truncation.
- `renderMarkdown()` in `packages/herdr/src/md-viewer.ts` is a mature, fully
  tested renderer used in the detail view.
- The metadata panel already supports scrolling via `metaScrollOffset`.
- Dynamic layout (`computeDynamicLayout`) ensures the selection list takes
  priority.

## Desired change

Replace `buildDescriptionPreview` with a markdown-aware preview function that:
1. Calls `renderMarkdown()` to produce styled terminal lines
2. Limits output to available panel space
3. Caches results keyed by (item.id, descriptionHash)
4. Integrates cleanly with existing `formatMetadataPanel` scrolling

## Related work

- **WL-0MSFZKQL700381P3** — Initial description preview (completed, raw lines)
- **`md-viewer.ts`** — Full markdown renderer used in detail view (already
  tested, no changes needed)
- **WL-0MSKFFJWD002BQJ5** — Use a proper markdown renderer for detail view
  description and md viewer (completed) — the direct precedent

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `buildDescriptionPreview()`, `formatMetadataPanel()`
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — description preview test suite
- `packages/herdr/src/md-viewer.ts` — `renderMarkdown()` (reference, no changes)

- **WL-0MSQ44MDX008U69J** — Herdr selection list: let list take as much space
  as it needs; metadata fills the rest and scrolls (the layout contract this
  change builds on: selection list keeps priority)

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Performance risk**: `renderMarkdown` runs the `marked` lexer on every
  selection change. Mitigated by caching keyed on (item.id, description hash).
- **Layout shift**: Rendered markdown lines may be taller/shorter than raw
  lines; the dynamic layout already absorbs this (list keeps priority).
- **ANSI truncation risk**: Rendered output contains ANSI escape sequences;
  truncation must not break sequences mid-code (existing `truncateLine`
  handles this).
- **Scope guard**: The preview remains display-only — note-edit chords
  (WL-0MSKV6SKK008MMXR) stay in the detail view's md viewer, NOT the metadata
  panel preview.
- **Cache invalidation assumption**: Description changes only via item refresh;
  cache cleared on refresh/selection change (no filesystem watch needed).

## Summary
Wire the DB-change gate into the scheduler tasks in runWorklistTui - skip unchanged ticks without spawning wl; keep all existing guards and manual paths.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. refresh tick: spawns zero wl processes when DB is unchanged since last cycle; runs normally when changed.
2. sync tick: skips wl sync when DB unchanged AND last successful sync (heartbeat marker) is fresher than maxSyncStalenessMs; otherwise runs doSync + doRefresh as today - still subject to heartbeat / single-flight / --if-idle guards.
3. resume-poll hidden-to-visible transition: applies the same DB-change gate.
4. Manual S (sync) and r (refresh) keypress paths are unchanged - always run.
5. First cycle after pane start always runs; signal-read failure fails open.
6. worklist.test.ts and auto-sync.test.ts cases from F1 pass.
7. README packages/herdr/README.md updated with maxSyncStalenessMs row and gate description.

## Minimal Implementation

- packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts:
  - Import DbChangeTracker from ./db-change.js.
  - Create tracker instance in runWorklistTui.
  - Refresh task: wrap doRefresh call with gate check.
  - Sync task: add staleness check with heartbeat freshness comparison.
  - Resume-poll: same gate as refresh tick.
  - Manual S/r: unchanged.
  - Code comments explaining the gate.
- packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts: expose staleness helper for the cap comparison.
- packages/herdr/README.md: document maxSyncStalenessMs and the DB-change gate.

## Dependencies
F2 (db-change module), F3 (maxSyncStalenessMs setting).

## Key Files
- packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts - scheduler task gate wiring.
- packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts - expose staleness helper.
- packages/herdr/README.md - settings table update + gate description.
